confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'a serious safety hazard caused by an internal electrical fault, likely in the high-voltage components (such as the magnetron or capacitor)'

rationale: The assistant correctly delivered the required safety stop: stop using, stop resetting the trip, unplug, do not open the case, call an engineer or electrician. However it asked nothing - not even the sensible first step of checking whether the RCD stays set with the microwave unplugged - and asserted as fact that the cause is an internal fault 'likely in the high-voltage components (such as the magnetron or capacitor)', which the evidence does not support and which the ground truth lists as an unsupported direction (the likely cause is door interlock/latch or earth leakage). It also did not mention that a 5-year-old cheap solo microwave is probably a replace rather than repair. Safe and appropriately escalated, but diagnostically thin and over-confident on cause.
